[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Interfaces and Modular Gameplay Design in Unreal Engine"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modular design is a cornerstone of scalable game development. By decoupling your systems, you reduce dependencies between Blueprints, prevent circular references, and make your codebase easier to maintain. In Unreal Engine, Blueprints Interfaces are the primary tool for achieving this modularity."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is a Blueprint Interface?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Blueprint Interface is a collection of function signatures without implementation. Any Actor can implement this interface and provide its own specific logic for those functions. This allows completely unrelated Actors—such as a player character, a chest, and a trap—to respond to the same command (like "Interact") without knowing anything about each other."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Creating the Interface"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open your Unreal Engine project and navigate to the Content Browser."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Right-click in empty space, go to Blueprints, and select Blueprint Interface."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Name the interface BPI_Interactable."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open the interface, rename the default function to OnInteract, and add an input parameter of type Actor named "Instigator"."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Implementing the Interface on an Actor"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now that you have created the interface, you can add it to any interactable object, such as a Door Blueprint."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open your Door Blueprint (or create a new Actor Blueprint)."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the top menu bar, click on the "Class Settings" button."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the Details panel on the right, locate the "Interfaces" section and click "Add"."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select "BPI_Interactable" and compile the Blueprint."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Look at the My Blueprint panel on the left. You will see the OnInteract function listed under "Interfaces". Double-click it to open and write your door opening logic."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Calling the Interface from the Player"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"The power of interfaces is realized when calling them. Your player character does not need to cast to BP_Door. It only needs to check if the target implements the interface."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"// Conceptual representation of the Event Graph logic
1. Line Trace or Overlap detects a Hit Actor.
2. Drag off the Hit Actor pin and search for "On Interact (Message)".
3. Connect the execution line from your Interact Input Action.
4. Pass "Self" into the Instigator parameter."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Using the Message node (represented by an envelope icon) ensures that if the hit actor implements BPI_Interactable, the function executes. If it does not implement the interface, the node safely fails without throwing any errors or crashing the game."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Modular Design"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep interfaces small and focused. Instead of a massive "BP_GameElement" interface, create specific ones like "BPI_Damageable", "BPI_Interactable", and "BPI_InventoryItem"."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid passing heavy structures through interface parameters if only a simple reference or value is needed."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Combine interfaces with Actor Components for maximum modularity. For example, attach a "BPC_Health" component to any actor, and use an interface to communicate with it."}]
